grade.first_issue: In the \(c\ne0\) case, several divisions by \(a\), \(a-c\), and \(f(b)\) are made without stating the necessary restrictions, and the resulting quadratic is initially asserted for every \(x\).
grade.summary: The classification \(f\equiv0\) or \(f(x)=c-x\) is correct, and the main arguments are sound. The omitted domain checks are directly repairable: \(f(c+f(b))=b-c\) and \(f(c)=0\) imply \(f(b)=0\) only when \(b=c\), while \(x=0,c\) are covered by the already known values \(f(0)=c\) and \(f(c)=0\).
strengths: The \(f(0)=0\) case correctly derives surjectivity and hence \(f(x)=-x\).
The nonzero-\(f(0)\) case obtains a valid quadratic restriction and successfully excludes mixed choices of its roots.
Both resulting families are checked directly in the original equation.

errors.description: The nonzero-\(f(0)\) derivation suppresses exceptional-value and nonvanishing checks needed to justify its divisions.
